text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Afeter 100 days in power, the ruling Homeland Union leader and chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbergis sees less socialism and more democracy in the country.
- The newspaper publishes an interview with Hungarian President Arpad Goncz whio starts today an official visit to Lithuania.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas supports the option that the state should own 34 percent of Butinge oil terminal.
- Vilnius prosecutor's office read its indictment to former finance minister Rolandas Matiliauskas, suspected of financial fraud.

- Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas appointed former defence minister Linas Linkevicius and former interior minister Virgilijus Bulovas to be his assistants. Linkevicius will advise Saudargas on NATO affairs and Bulovas on questions of internal policy.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius says that the Butinge oil terminal is not a strategic but a commercial object.
- The opposition Lithuanian Democratioc Labour party says they see no better candidate to the presidential post than Algirdas Brazauskas.
